chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah support him—informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Abū al-Jawzāʾ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

If a man dies while traveling with women, and among them he has neither his wife nor a woman within the unmarriageable kinship degree, they should wrap him from the waist down to the knees, pour water over him, not look at his private parts, not touch him with their hands, and purify him.

key_terms.الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ: the knees; the extent of the covering mentioned here
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the circumstance in which this ruling applies
key_terms.ذَاتُ مَحْرَمٍ: a woman related within prohibited degrees of marriage; one whose presence changes the ruling
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهِ: his private parts; the area that must not be looked at
key_terms.يَلْمِسْنَهُ: they touch him; an act prohibited here with the hands
key_terms.يُؤَزِّرْنَهُ: they cover or wrap him around the lower body
key_terms.يُطَهِّرْنَهُ: they purify him; referring to the ritual cleansing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: How should women wash a deceased man during travel if his wife or mahram is not present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for handling the body of a deceased man when only unrelated women are present during travel. It instructs them to preserve his ʿawrah, avoid direct looking and touching, and perform the necessary purification by pouring water over him.
